subject: Lognormal prior for fixed effect parameter

messages.author: a38e579a8decc4d1
messages.subject: Lognormal prior for fixed effect parameter
parts:
I need to restrict the values of a fixed effect parameter to only negative values.  The parameter is the regression coefficient for the quadratic effect of one of the explanatory variables in a random slope Poisson regression with an ar1 model for the random effects.  Without such a restrictions the posterior distributions for other quantities of interest (which involve this parameter in the denominator) would basically not make much sense.  So the idea would be to build this restriction into the prior (perhaps after first checking if a negative quadratic effect is supported by the data).

I'm aware of the control.fixed argument which could be used to specify normal priors on the fixed effects but we think it would make more sense (within the biological context) to think about this parameter as a form of scale parameter which would suggest that a vague lognormal prior (for the negative value) may be more sensible.

To implement this, we are currently sampling from the joint posterior using inla.posterior.sample() and then using rejecting sampling such that the resulting distribution corresponds to our desired choice of prior.  This is obviously somewhat inefficient however if using a large variance for the lognormal making the rejection probability very high.

So I'm wondering if there is any other way getting around this problem?

Jarle Tufto
